rationale: GE-WERIAN is closely related to OE *werian* "to clothe/dress," and in the context of investiture, it carries the sense of formally clothing or endowing someone with power or authority (as kings or emperors do). The synset invest.v.03 ("furnish with power or authority; of kings or emperors") best captures this ceremonial, regal sense of conferring authority, which aligns with the Old English usage and the likely Latin anchor *investire*.
